card.name: Bachata
card.era: 20th century; first single recorded 30 May 1962 (Jose Manuel Calderon)
card.tagline: Romantic Dominican guitar music and sensual partner dance.
card.profile: Bachata is a Dominican music-and-dance tradition that emerged in the 20th century from a fusion of rhythmic bolero with Afro-Antillean genres (Cuban son, cha-cha-cha, merengue). The dance is a couple's dance with sensual hip movement and a simple eight-step structure (side, side, tap/'pop'), in open or closed position. The typical group has five instruments: requinto (lead guitar), segunda (rhythm guitar), bass, bongos and guira. Lyrics express love and nostalgia; once stigmatized as 'musica de amargue' before globalizing via Juan Luis Guerra, Aventura and Romeo Santos (UNESCO; English Wikipedia).
card.insight: UNESCO inscribed 'Music and dance of Dominican Bachata' on the Representative List in 2019 (file 01514, decision 14.COM 10.b.10); whereas the merengue bid took 12 years, the bachata bid was expedited in two (Listin Diario via DR1.com, 2019; UNESCO).
